008package paint.shared.utils;
009
010import org.apache.commons.math3.fitting.leastsquares.*;
011import org.apache.commons.math3.linear.Array2DRowRealMatrix;
012import org.apache.commons.math3.linear.ArrayRealVector;
013import org.apache.commons.math3.linear.DiagonalMatrix;
014import org.apache.commons.math3.util.FastMath;
015import paint.shared.objects.Track;
016
017import java.util.Arrays;
018import java.util.List;
019import java.util.Map;
020import java.util.TreeMap;
021
022import static java.lang.Double.NaN;
023
024public class CalculateTau {
025
026    private CalculateTau() {
027    }
028
029    /**
030     * Calculates the tau (time constant) and goodness-of-fit (R-squared) from a given set of track durations using an exponential decay model.
031     * The method performs a series of checks and validations, fits the data to a model,
032     * and evaluates the quality of the fit to decide the result status.
033     *
034     * @param tracks              the list of Track objects from which durations are extracted. Each Track represents a single time measurement.
035     *                            points status.
036     * @param minRequiredRSquared the minimum allowable value for the R-squared of the fit. If the computed R-squared is less than this threshold, the method will return a too-low
037     *                            R-squared status.
038     * @return a {@code CalculateTauResult} object containing the calculated tau, R-squared value, and the status of the calculation. Possible statuses include success, insufficient
039     * points, no fit, or R-squared too low.
040     */
041    public static CalculateTauResult calculateTau(List<Track> tracks,
042            double minRequiredRSquared) {
043
044        // 1) Extract durations
045        final int n = tracks.size();
046        double[] durations = new double[n];
047        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
048            durations[i] = tracks.get(i).getTrackDuration();
049        }
050
051        // 2) Build frequency distribution (sorted by duration)
052        Map<Double, Integer> freq = createFrequencyDistribution(durations);
053
054        // Need at least 2 distinct x-values to fit
055        if (freq.size() < 2) {
056            return new CalculateTauResult(0.0, 0.0, CalculateTauResult.Status.TAU_NO_FIT);
057        }
058
059        // 3) Convert to arrays for fitting
060        double[] x = new double[freq.size()];
061        double[] y = new double[freq.size()];
062        int k = 0;
063        for (Map.Entry<Double, Integer> e : freq.entrySet()) {
064            x[k] = e.getKey();
065            y[k] = e.getValue();
066            k++;
067        }
068
069        // 4) Fit and evaluate quality
070        CalculateTauExpDecayFitter.FitResult fitResult = CalculateTauExpDecayFitter.fit(x, y);
071
072        // 5) Reject non-finite results
073        if (!Double.isFinite(fitResult.rSquared) || !Double.isFinite(fitResult.tauMs)) {
074            return new CalculateTauResult(fitResult.tauMs, fitResult.rSquared, CalculateTauResult.Status.TAU_NO_FIT);
075        }
076
077        // 6) Apply threshold
078        if (fitResult.rSquared < minRequiredRSquared) {
079            return new CalculateTauResult(fitResult.tauMs, fitResult.rSquared, CalculateTauResult.Status.TAU_RSQUARED_TOO_LOW);
080        }
081
082        return new CalculateTauResult(fitResult.tauMs, fitResult.rSquared, CalculateTauResult.Status.TAU_SUCCESS);
083    }
084
085    /**
086     * Represents the result of the tau calculation process, containing the
087     * tau value, R-squared value, and the status of the calculation.
088     * <p>
089     * This result is produced after performing an exponential decay model
090     * fitting on given track durations, evaluating the quality of the fit,
091     * and determining if the computation meets the required conditions.
092     */
093    public static class CalculateTauResult {
094
095        private final double tau;
096        private final double rsquared;
097        private final Status status;
098
099        public CalculateTauResult(double tau, double rsquared, Status status) {
100            this.tau      = tau;
101            this.rsquared = rsquared;
102            this.status   = status;
103        }
104
105        public enum Status {
106            TAU_SUCCESS,
107            TAU_RSQUARED_TOO_LOW,
108            TAU_NO_FIT
109        }
110
111        public double getTau() {
112            return tau;
113        }
114
115        public double getRSquared() {
116            return rsquared;
117        }
118
119        public Status getStatus() {
120            return status;
121        }
122    }
123
124    /**
125     * Creates a frequency distribution from an array of track durations.
126     * The method calculates the number of occurrences for each unique duration
127     * and stores the result in a map where the keys are unique durations and
128     * the values are their respective frequencies.
129     *
130     * @param trackDurations an array of double values representing track durations.
131     *                       If the array is null, an empty map is returned.
132     * @return a map containing unique track durations as keys and their
133     * corresponding frequencies as values.
134     */
135    private static Map<Double, Integer> createFrequencyDistribution(double[] trackDurations) {
136        Map<Double, Integer> frequencyDistribution = new TreeMap<>();
137        if (trackDurations == null) {
138            return frequencyDistribution;
139        }
140
141        for (double duration : trackDurations) {
142            Integer prev = frequencyDistribution.get(duration);
143            frequencyDistribution.put(duration, (prev == null ? 1 : prev + 1));
144        }
145        return frequencyDistribution;
146    }
147
148    /**
149     * A utility class performing exponential decay fitting. This class enables
150     * the computation of an exponential decay's time constant (tau) and
151     * the goodness-of-fit (R-squared) through least-squares optimization.
152     */
153    private static class CalculateTauExpDecayFitter {
154
155        private CalculateTauExpDecayFitter() {
156        }
157
158        /**
159         * Immutable fit result.
160         */
161        private static final class FitResult {
162            final double tauMs;
163            final double rSquared;
164
165            FitResult(double tauMs, double rSquared) {
166                this.tauMs = tauMs;
167                this.rSquared = rSquared;
168            }
169        }
170
171        /**
172         * Fits a model to the given data points using a non-linear least squares optimization
173         * and returns the results as a {@code FitResult}.
174         * The model assumes an exponential decay function of the form:
175         * y = m * exp(-t * x) + b.
176         *
177         * @param x the independent variable data points (input values)
178         * @param y the dependent variable data points (output values)
179         *          Both arrays must have the same length and contain at least two elements.
180         * @return a {@code FitResult} containing the calculated time constant in milliseconds (tauMs)
181         * and the coefficient of determination (rSquared).
182         * Returns a {@code FitResult} with NaN values if the input is invalid
183         * or the fitting process fails.
184         */
185        private static FitResult fit(double[] x, double[] y) {
186            if (x == null || y == null || x.length != y.length || x.length < 2) {
187                return new FitResult(NaN, NaN);
188            }
189
190            final MultivariateJacobianFunction model = p -> {
191                double m = p.getEntry(0);
192                double t = p.getEntry(1);
193                double b = p.getEntry(2);
194
195                double[] values = new double[x.length];
196                double[][] jac = new double[x.length][3];
197
198                for (int i = 0; i < x.length; i++) {
199                    double e = FastMath.exp(-t * x[i]);
200                    values[i] = m * e + b;
201                    jac[i][0] = e;              // d/dm
202                    jac[i][1] = -m * x[i] * e;  // d/dt
203                    jac[i][2] = 1.0;            // d/db
204                }
205                return new org.apache.commons.math3.util.Pair<>(
206                        new ArrayRealVector(values, false),
207                        new Array2DRowRealMatrix(jac, false)
208                );
209            };
210
211            double[] p0 = initialGuess(x, y);
212            double[] w = new double[y.length];
213            Arrays.fill(w, 1.0);
214
215            LeastSquaresProblem problem = new LeastSquaresBuilder()
216                    .start(p0)
217                    .model(model)
218                    .target(y)
219                    .weight(new DiagonalMatrix(w))
220                    .maxEvaluations(10_000)
221                    .maxIterations(1_000)
222                    .build();
223
224            try {
225                LeastSquaresOptimizer.Optimum opt =
226                        new LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer().optimize(problem);
227
228                double[] p = opt.getPoint().toArray();
229                double m = p[0], t = p[1], b = p[2];
230                double tauMs = (t > 0.0) ? (1000.0 / t) : NaN;
231                double r2 = computeRSquared(x, y, m, t, b);
232
233                return new FitResult(tauMs, r2);
234            } catch (Throwable ignored) {
235                return new FitResult(NaN, NaN);
236            }
237        }
238
239        /**
240         * Generates an initial guess for the parameters of an exponential decay model
241         * based on the provided input data.
242         * This method calculates preliminary values for the model parameters
243         * which can be used as a starting point for further optimization or fitting.
244         *
245         * @param x the independent variable data points (input values).
246         *          The array must have at least two elements.
247         * @param y the dependent variable data points (output values).
248         *          The array must have the same length as the {@code x} array.
249         * @return a double array containing the initial guesses for the model parameters:
250         * - {@code m}: the scaling factor
251         * - {@code t}: the time constant
252         * - {@code b}: the baseline offset
253         */
254        private static double[] initialGuess(double[] x, double[] y) {
255            double minY = Arrays.stream(y).min().orElse(0);
256            double maxY = Arrays.stream(y).max().orElse(1);
257            double maxX = Arrays.stream(x).max().orElse(1);
258
259            double b = Math.max(0.0, minY);
260            double m = Math.max(1e-6, maxY - b);
261
262            double eps  = Math.max(1e-6, 0.01 * m);
263            double sumX = 0, sumXX = 0, sumY = 0, sumXY = 0;
264            int    n    = 0;
265
266            for (int i = 0; i < x.length; i++) {
267                double yiAdj = y[i] - b;
268                if (yiAdj > eps) {
269                    double lx = x[i];
270                    double ly = FastMath.log(yiAdj);
271                    sumX += lx;
272                    sumXX += lx * lx;
273                    sumY += ly;
274                    sumXY += lx * ly;
275                    n++;
276                }
277            }
278
279            double t;
280            if (n >= 2) {
281                double denominator = (n * sumXX - sumX * sumX);
282                double slope = (denominator == 0.0)
283                        ? -1.0
284                        : (n * sumXY - sumX * sumY) / denominator;
285                t = Math.max(1e-9, -slope);
286            } else {
287                t = 1.0 / Math.max(1e-3, maxX);
288            }
289
290            // Clamp to reasonable ranges
291            m = clamp(m, 1e-9, 1e9);
292            t = clamp(t, 1e-9, 1e3);
293            b = clamp(b, 0.0, Math.max(1.0, maxY));
294
295            return new double[]{m, t, b};
296        }
297
298        /**
299         * Computes the coefficient of determination (R-squared) for the given data points
300         * and model parameters. The R-squared value indicates how well the model fits
301         * the data, with a value ranging from 0 (no fit) to 1 (perfect fit).
302         *
303         * @param x the independent variable data points (input values).
304         *          Must be an array of doubles with length matching the {@code y} array.
305         * @param y the dependent variable data points (output values).
306         *          Must be an array of doubles with length matching the {@code x} array.
307         * @param m the scaling factor (model parameter).
308         * @param t the time constant (model parameter).
309         * @param b the baseline offset (model parameter).
310         * @return the R-squared value, representing the goodness of fit of the model to the data.
311         * Returns NaN if the total sum of squares is zero.
312         */
313        private static double computeRSquared(double[] x, double[] y, double m, double t, double b) {
314            double meanY  = Arrays.stream(y).average().orElse(0);
315            double ssRes  = 0.0;
316            double  ssTot = 0.0;
317            for (int i = 0; i < y.length; i++) {
318                double predicted = m * FastMath.exp(-t * x[i]) + b;
319                ssRes += Math.pow(y[i] - predicted, 2);
320                ssTot += Math.pow(y[i] - meanY, 2);
321            }
322            return (ssTot == 0.0) ? NaN : 1.0 - (ssRes / ssTot);
323        }
324
325        private static double clamp(double v, double lo, double hi) {
326            return Math.max(lo, Math.min(hi, v));
327        }
328    }
329
330    /**
331     * Fits the given data arrays to an exponential decay model and returns the calculated time constant (tau)
332     * and the goodness-of-fit (R-squared) as an array of double values.
333     *
334     * @param x the independent variable data points
335     * @param y the dependent variable data points
336     * @return an array of double values, where the first element is the time constant (tau) and the second
337     * element is the goodness-of-fit (R-squared)
338     */
339    public static double[] debugFit(double[] x, double[] y) {
340        CalculateTauExpDecayFitter.FitResult result = CalculateTauExpDecayFitter.fit(x, y);
341        return new double[]{result.tauMs, result.rSquared};
342    }
343}
